governing_intent: Build the smallest canonical-Python substrate that can actually reach the provisioned SWF-08 sandbox — installation-token acquisition and refresh, live repository and Projects v2 read, fenced one-way projection write, resident authenticated webhook ingress, sandbox profile composition and live `doctor` transport probes — and prove it independently and locally-repeatably, so that PY-10 enters its single coherent live proof with transport defects already removed from the failure surface.
summary: Assessed at clean `main` de2113d. The one owner clarification that held the previous assessment (PY-09B.assessment.json, baseline 30d0703) is closed, by Founder action rather than by rewording. `contents: write` is granted to installation 163346526 and the correction is recorded with its reasoning at docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:55 and :62-88; binding rule 4 (docs/work-units/python/PY-09B.md:36-38) now pins the four-permission set and states why the Node bootstrap's three-permission set is not the correct baseline for this architecture; AC 2 (:84) now requires `contents: write` explicitly and requires `contents: read` alone to fail, which closes the exact-set check against the half-grant. The grant is not asserted from a permission list: docs/evidence/py10-preflight-2026-09-21-pre-contents-grant.json, -negative-control.json and -post-contents-grant.json record passing-against-the-wrong-spec, failing-against-the-right-one (2/17, on exactly the two permission checks) and passing-against-the-right-one, and docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:90-105 records a live clone/commit/push/fresh-clone read-back against the private sandbox repository with the installation credential. AC 3 and the passing half of AC 9's source-control probe are therefore now satisfiable, and doctor.py:165's `'contents:write' in publication_permissions` requirement is reachable. The SWF-34 amendment from the prior cycle stands intact: binding rule 6 (:40-44), scope item 8 (:56) and AC 10 (:92-95) separate a permission-enforced repository boundary from a configuration-enforced Project boundary, forbid claiming token-level Project isolation, and name PY-10 AC 16 as the compensating control — matching docs/decisions/2026-09-21-sandbox-isolation-standard.md exactly. The verifier's obligation to execute the bounded live portion itself on the provisioned host is explicit at :103. The BIU's premise remains factually true against this tree: github_work_management.py:16 takes `snapshot` and `projection_write` as injected callables with no HTTP path; github_webhook.py:99 binds 127.0.0.1:0 inside a test-helper contextmanager; installation/domain/github_profile.py:13-21 carries no App identity, installation id, bind address or port; composition/doctor_probes.py supplies only Git-worktree and worker-executable evidence; pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency. The boundary against the capstone is clean and mutually declared — PY-10.md scope item 1 says 'PY-10 builds none of it' while retaining the obligation to verify it end to end — and PY-09B rule 7 refuses the backlog seed and the factory loop. Intent, non-goals, twelve observable acceptance criteria, the offline/bounded-live/proven-red iteration surface SWF-33 demanded, and honest requirement extents ('the first **live** GitHub adapter behind the existing port') are all present. Everything an implementation agent now faces is research inside constraints that already exist.
implementation_unknowns: How to mint the App JWT. pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency and the stdlib has no RS256 signing, so the choice between a first adapter-layer dependency (PyJWT/cryptography, which the bootstrap preflight already uses) and shelling out to openssl is ordinary engineering. The fitness vendor-signature check bans vendor types only in domain/ports signatures, so either is permitted at the adapter boundary.

The shape of the live GitHub client behind the existing ports: REST for app/installation/token/repository/issues/permissions, GraphQL for Projects v2 field and option identities, inside the PY-05 port contracts (execution_coordination/ports/work_management.py) and the hexagonal adapter rules that already constrain it.

How the fence is realized. Projects v2 offers no compare-and-set on `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`, so 'carries the expected revision and refuses on conflict' must be canonical-side fencing plus read-back — which is what FD-01 requires and what github_work_management.py:59-75 already demonstrates against its own revision map.

How AC 2's simulated extra grant, missing grant and `contents: read`-alone cases are constructed. The App cannot be reconfigured by an agent, so these are fixture-level simulations of the live permission response against an exact-set comparator — the shape the bootstrap preflight already demonstrates at docs/evidence/py10-preflight-2026-09-21-negative-control.json, reimplemented in canonical Python because the preflight script is bootstrap and out of scope.

How to originate a real signed delivery repeatably for AC 7. With `issues: read` the App cannot self-trigger an `issue_comment`, and `contents: write` does not help because `push` is not a subscribed event; the one App-writable in-band trigger is the Project field update from scope item 4, which emits the subscribed `projects_v2_item`. Whether GitHub redelivers an installation's own Project writes to that installation needs empirical confirmation, with the already-proven manual comment trigger (docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:152-163) as fallback.

Extending GitHubProfile with App identity, installation id, private-key reference, ingress bind address and port while keeping doctor's `_configuration` check (doctor.py:117-125) meaningful, and how the profile factory locates ~/.config/alienintent-sandbox/profile.json without embedding installation detail in source — composition is the only layer the fitness `configuration` check permits to read the environment.

How the resident ingress is started and stopped for the bounded live checks without entering PY-10 territory. `serve_webhook` (github_webhook.py:86-107) is a test-helper contextmanager on an ephemeral port and FactoryCoordinator.start() is a synchronous drain. The smallest sufficient answer under SWF-20 is a bounded harness-owned server lifetime bound to the profile's configured host and port, not a new long-running command.

How the live portion is kept out of the default collected suite (markers or an env-gated skip) so AC 12 holds on a runner with no sandbox credentials. .github/workflows/python-architecture-fitness.yml runs `pip install pytest` then `pytest -q` with no project install and no credentials, and tests/ contains no skip/marker gating convention to copy.

Where the redacted evidence is retained. The contract names no path; the repository convention is docs/evidence/ (PY-01, PY-06, PY-07 and the three preflight JSONs are all there), while docs/verification/ is PY-10's mandate and does not yet exist.

A stable non-reversible way to prove 'the run used the sandbox identity' (AC 11) without emitting App ID, installation ID or hostname — for example a salted digest of the identifiers compared against the profile. Note that AC 10b independently requires the evidence to name the exact Project targeted, and the Project node id is not among the identifiers rule 3 forbids.

How the live source-control probe derives `publication_permissions` from an authenticated observation rather than an adapter constant, so AC 9's 'no probe can pass on an adapter-declared flag alone' holds against doctor.py:161-168.
verification_assessment: Real executable proof rather than description, and better sequenced than any prior BIU in this cohort. Every capability in scope carries a named negative control — invalid or missing credential reference, simulated extra grant, simulated missing grant, `contents: read` alone, stale projection write, unsigned/wrong-signature/replayed delivery, fail-closed Project identity resolution, a failing case for each doctor probe — and AC 5, AC 7, AC 9 and AC 10b require proven-red demonstration (remove the fence, use the wrong secret, deny an adapter-declared pass) in line with SWF-24. The offline/bounded-live split is stated rather than assumed, which is what SWF-33 demanded, and the verification-first repair sequencing clause is satisfiable because the fixture-backed harness can exist before any live call. Independence is now explicit at :103: the verifier executes the bounded live portion itself on the provisioned host against the same identities and re-runs the offline portion in full. The permission criterion is no longer describing something the environment cannot provide — the three preflight snapshots plus the live clone/push/read-back record show the check goes red without the grant and green with it, which is exactly the discrimination SWF-24 asks for. Two residual weaknesses, both implementation-side. First, AC 12's 'the Python suite passes' collides with a CI job that installs only pytest on a hosted runner with no credentials and never installs the project, so the live/offline boundary must be mechanized and any new dependency must reach that workflow. Second, AC 11's redaction obligation sits against AC 7's requirement to prove the delivery arrived through the provisioned endpoint and AC 10b's requirement that evidence name the targeted Project; the scheme must not destroy the isolation proof it protects, and rule 3 governs what this BIU produces — it is not licence to redact docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md or the committed preflight JSONs, which legitimately publish App and installation identifiers as provisioning records.
material_risks: Widening GitHubProfile ripples through doctor's `_configuration` check (doctor.py:117-125), both composition roots (composition/github_profile.py, composition/offline_profile.py) and the existing profile tests, so a defect in the profile shape is the one failure mode in this BIU that is not module-local.

Introducing the repository's first runtime dependency requires a matching change to .github/workflows/python-architecture-fitness.yml, which installs only pytest and never installs the project — unnamed work that SWF-20 makes a mechanically detectable verification finding unless treated as lifecycle-necessary for AC 12. Shelling out to openssl avoids the dependency but adds a process-level precondition the CI runner must still satisfy.

AC 7 depends on GitHub redelivering an event the installation itself caused. If it does not, the only repeatable in-band trigger disappears (the App cannot comment with `issues: read`, and `push` is not subscribed) and the 'bounded, repeatable, individually diagnosable' property SWF-33 required degrades toward a manual one-shot — which also weakens the verifier's ability to execute the live portion independently as :103 requires.

Binding rule 3 forbids App ID, installation ID and hostname in source, tests, logs, diagnostics and evidence, while docs/evidence/py10-preflight-*.json commit exactly those values (app_id=5014629, installation_id=163346526, the key path) and docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md commits the hostname. A verifier reading AC 11 mechanically across docs/evidence/ could raise a finding against records this BIU neither produced nor may modify; the provenance boundary should be stated in the retained evidence rather than resolved by redacting provisioning records.

Scope item 5's 'resident' ingress has no home in the current CLI, and the boundary between a bounded harness-owned server and a new long-running service sits directly against rule 7's non-goal — the cheapest correct answer risks reading as under-delivery, the fuller one as scope expansion under SWF-20.

`contents: write` genuinely widens the sandbox token's blast radius on the sandbox repository (it can now push and force-branch), which is the accepted cost of the custody invariant. It changes nothing about repository selection, so isolation evidence under AC 10a is unaffected, but the isolation evidence must not be written as if the grant were still read-only.

The organization-wide `organization_projects` grant remains an accepted residual risk (SWF-34); AC 10b must be implemented as deterministic fail-closed addressing and must not drift back into a token-scope claim during repair.
SWF-09 applies: the invocation path used for the live checks may report neither token nor monetary cost, which must be recorded UNKNOWN and never assumed zero.

This factory has accepted 0 of 7 Wave 1 implementation BIUs first-pass (docs/evidence/wave1-repair-cycles.md). READY reduces the decision risk, not the repair risk; the verification-first sequencing clause at :70-79 is the control that matters and should be enforced literally on the first repair cycle.
next_action: Release PY-09B to IMPLEMENT through normal SWF-21 admission at baseline de2113d, with no contract amendment required. Direct the implementer to build the fixture-backed harness (token expiry/refresh, exact-permission comparator including the `contents: read`-alone case, field/option resolution, fenced-write conflict, signature verification, delivery deduplication) before any live call, and to settle three mechanical choices in the first cycle and record them in the candidate: the live/offline test gating mechanism and any matching change to .github/workflows/python-architecture-fitness.yml, the retained-evidence path (docs/evidence/ per repository convention, leaving docs/verification/ to PY-10), and the non-reversible sandbox-identity attestation that satisfies AC 11 without weakening AC 7 or AC 10b.
rationale: The single blocking question from the previous assessment was closed the way it should have been — by a Founder decision plus live proof, not by softening the criterion. The grant was made and re-accepted, the operations record was corrected with the reasoning preserved rather than overwritten, binding rule 4 and AC 2 were amended to match, and the capability the grant exists for was demonstrated end to end against the private repository with the installation credential. The three preflight snapshots are the strongest evidence in this BIU's file: they show the check passing against a wrong specification, failing against the corrected one, and passing again — which is exactly the failure mode SWF-24 and SWF-34 named as durable lessons, caught and closed rather than carried into a repair cycle. With that resolved, every decision input this contract depends on is closed: SWF-08 provisioned and verified the target, SWF-09 fixes budget policy, SWF-33 fixes the decomposition and the iteration surface, SWF-34 fixes the isolation standard, FD-01 fixes projection direction, FD-02 through FD-06 and the Architecture Authority constrain the implementation, and PY-05, PY-06, PY-08 and PY-09 are accepted and on main. What remains is research inside existing constraints — which JWT path, which GraphQL queries, how to gate live tests, how to bound the ingress lifetime, where evidence lands — and none of it is owner work. There is still no case for splitting: outbound API access and inbound ingress share one profile, one credential path and one set of doctor probes, and the only repeatable in-band way to originate a real delivery runs through the projection write, so the two halves verify each other rather than standing apart. Rework locality is MEDIUM rather than LOW only because the profile shape is the one surface that reaches doctor, both composition roots and existing tests at once; everything else is additive adapter work behind ports that already exist.
